canDos.text: Read shop signs with opening hours and work out when you can go together.

check.instructions: It's Wednesday, 12:30. Read the four signs on your street and answer the questions.

questions.q: Can you two go to the café this afternoon?
You need the post office on Saturday morning. What is the problem?
When can you go into the watch shop today?

canDos.text: Make simple requests in a shop: ask the clerk to wait, to put things in a bag, or to write the price down.

check.instructions: You're buying towels. The AI plays the clerk and says the lines below, one at a time. Reply to each with a polite request using 〜てください: (1) you didn't catch the price, so ask them to write it down; (2) ask them to wait while you check with your partner; (3) ask them to put the towels in a bag.
check.material:
いらっしゃいませ。このタオルは{二千|にせん}{四百|よんひゃく}{円|えん}です。
こちらでいいですか。
{袋|ふくろ}はどうしますか。
rubric: Asks for the price in writing: 書いてください
Asks the clerk to wait: ちょっと待ってください
Asks for a bag: 袋に入れてください
Opens politely with すみません and keeps to です / ます with the clerk

canDos.text: Compare things with your partner while shopping (this one's good, it's not very expensive, that's really big) and choose one.

check.instructions: You and your partner (or the AI) are choosing a new pillow. Look at the three below. In casual Japanese, comment on at least two of them with degree words, say which one you won't buy, and agree on one (どれがいい？ — これがいい).
rubric: Uses とても / すごく / ちょっと with an adjective (ちょっと高い)
Uses あまり or 全然 with a negative (あまり高くない)
Says what they won't buy in the plain negative (Aは買わない)
Asks or answers with が: どれがいい？ — これがいい

canDos.text: Follow a casual chat about what to buy and what you don't need, and tick off a shopping list.

check.instructions: Listen to a couple deciding what to buy at the supermarket (two voices, taking turns). Their list says 牛乳, 卵, パン, 石けん and お菓子. Then answer the questions.
check.material:
スーパーで{何|なに}{買|か}う？
えっと、{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}がない。{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}は{買|か}う。
{卵|たまご}は？
{卵|たまご}は{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}にあるよ。{今日|きょう}は{買|か}わない。
パンは？ {二|ふた}つ{買|か}う？
ううん、{一|ひと}つだけ。あ、それから、トイレの{石|せっ}けんがない。
じゃあ、{石|せっ}けんも。お{菓子|かし}は？
お{菓子|かし}は{買|か}わない！ うちにたくさんあるよ。

questions.q: Which item do they decide not to buy today?
How much bread do they buy?
Why don't they buy any sweets?
options: There are still lots at home

task.goal: Buy new towels and cups for home for under 5,000 yen: compare the options, agree which ones are best, and ask the clerk (played by the AI) to put them in a bag.
task.outcomeQuestion: What did you buy, and how much was it altogether?

roles.a: Sees the shelf with the options and prices (card A)
roles.b: Knows the budget, what's already at home and what you need (card B)

task.infoA: Card A — you're at the shelf. Towels (タオル): ① big, ¥1,800 each; ② small, ¥600 each; ③ big and really soft (すごくいい), ¥3,000 each. Cups (コップ): ④ glass, ¥500 each; ⑤ big and a bit heavy (ちょっと重い), ¥900 each. All prices include tax (税込). Describe the options with とても / すごく / ちょっと and あまり〜ない, and give the prices.
task.infoB: Card B — you know what you need. Budget: up to ¥5,000 altogether (五千円まで). You have lots of small towels at home, so you won't buy those (小さいタオルは買わない); you need two big ones (大きいタオルを二枚). You need two cups (コップを二つ), and you don't like heavy cups (重いコップはあまり好きじゃない). Ask which ones are good (どれがいい？) and how much they are, add up the total, and finish by asking the clerk to put everything in a bag (袋に入れてください).
task.twist: Repeat it 2–7 days later with a ¥4,000 budget and a sale: the soft towels (③) are now half price, ¥1,500 each. Redo the maths and choose again; this time the clerk also asks how you will pay (カードですか、現金ですか).
task.aiRole: The shop clerk: greets you, answers price questions politely, and bags the items when asked (いらっしゃいませ / 袋はどうしますか).

scripted.jp: タオルはこの{三|みっ}つ。どれがいい？
scripted.en: These are the three towels. Which do you like?

scripted.jp: {大|おお}きいタオルを{二枚|にまい}{買|か}う。{小|ちい}さいタオルは{買|か}わない。うちにたくさんあるよ。
scripted.en: Let's get two big towels. Not the small ones — we have lots at home.

scripted.jp: {大|おお}きいタオルはこれとこれ。これは{千|せん}{八百|はっぴゃく}{円|えん}。これは{三千|さんぜん}{円|えん}。すごくいいよ。
scripted.en: The big ones are this and this. This one's 1,800 yen. This one's 3,000 yen, and it's really nice.

scripted.jp: {三千|さんぜん}{円|えん}？ ちょっと{高|たか}い。{五千|ごせん}{円|えん}までだよ。
scripted.en: 3,000 yen? That's a bit pricey. We can only spend up to 5,000 yen.

scripted.jp: そうか。じゃあ、{千|せん}{八百|はっぴゃく}{円|えん}のタオルにする？
scripted.en: Right. Then shall we go with the 1,800-yen towels?

scripted.jp: うん、それがいい。コップは？
scripted.en: Yes, those are good. What about cups?

scripted.jp: {五百|ごひゃく}{円|えん}のコップと{九百|きゅうひゃく}{円|えん}のコップがある。{九百|きゅうひゃく}{円|えん}のコップはちょっと{重|おも}いよ。
scripted.en: There are 500-yen cups and 900-yen cups. The 900-yen ones are a bit heavy.

scripted.jp: {重|おも}いコップはあまり{好|す}きじゃない。{五百|ごひゃく}{円|えん}のコップを{二|ふた}つ{買|か}う。
scripted.en: I'm not keen on heavy cups. Let's get two of the 500-yen ones.
So how much does that come to?

scripted.jp: えっと…{三千|さんぜん}{六百|ろっぴゃく}{円|えん}と{千|せん}{円|えん}。{四千|よんせん}{六百|ろっぴゃく}{円|えん}だね。{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}！
scripted.en: Um… 3,600 and 1,000. So 4,600 yen. We're fine!

scripted.jp: よかった。すみません、これをください。
scripted.en: Great. Excuse me, we'll take these.

scripted.jp: それから、{袋|ふくろ}に{入|い}れてください。
scripted.en: And could you put them in a bag, please?

capstone.title: Saturday at the shops
capstone.brief: Go shopping together for the house. Check when the shop opens and closes, compare items (which is better? is it very expensive?), say in casual Japanese what you don't need, make two requests to the clerk, and decide what to buy.
